answer.rationale: The mandate requires an 18% cost cut and the low-cost vendor quote meets it, but switching primary supply with only a 14-day runway and zero production buffer (94% of committed volume) risks a delivery disruption that would far outweigh the savings if onboarding hiccups occur. Memory_c4 indicates that using a credible market benchmark (here, the low-cost vendor's quote) to renegotiate with the incumbent previously recovered real margin and improved terms without any integration disruption, consistent with c1's finding that incumbent continuity avoids migration risk. Before committing, I want to verify c4's archived record to see the actual magnitude of savings achieved, since the consolidated summary doesn't state whether it came close to an 18%-scale reduction — if it fell well short, negotiation alone won't satisfy finance's mandate and a second-source or partial switch may be needed next cycle. I'm flagging downstream risk because negotiated savings may not fully close the gap to 18%, meaning this single-cycle decision could leave residual cost-mandate risk unresolved, and I'm treating the low-cost vendor's proven cost/onboarding record as unverified regarding delivery reliability under tight-capacity conditions, since none of the memories directly address vendor performance when the line has no slack.
